claims.claim: Reachability is exactly a sparse unary congruence-closure query.
claims.evidence: Let R relate wires joined by a well-nested path that leaves an untouched baseline stack unchanged. R is an equivalence. If edges (o,X,t) and (o',X,t') have t R t', pushing X along the first edge, following the R-path, and reversing the second edge gives o R o'; hence the least stable equivalence θ is contained in R. Conversely, decompose any well-nested path into concatenated primitive excursions: induction on nesting and length, using the same folding rule and transitivity, gives R contained in θ. An execution starting above the bottom symbol cannot underflow before done, so exit reachability is exactly whether the start is θ-equivalent to an outer-pin wire. Pins select edges but the box X is the only pushed symbol, so suppressing pins in the closure key is valid.
claims.witness: The mutually inverse constructions are a folding derivation from each balanced maze path and a balanced maze path from each folding derivation.
claims.search_method: Independently derived the balanced-path characterization from the authorized source model, then exhaustively compared fixed-point closure with the sparse event algorithm on 328210 small box-labelled graphs using integer operations only.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic O(B+(W+E) log(W+E))-time, O(W+E+B)-space algorithm, eliminating the dense W·B initialization.
claims.evidence: For each current target class C, D_C retains one original edge per box. Every duplicate key identifies exactly a forced merge of its two origins. Conversely, melding D_C and D_D after a class merge reports every newly enabled folding rule. Thus every performed union belongs to θ, while the terminal partition is stable; leastness then proves equality with θ. Every collision discards one retained original edge, so at most E events are created. Initial two-key radix sorting and map construction cost O(W+E+B). Smaller-to-larger member relabeling costs O(W log W). A balanced-tree meld of sizes m≤n costs O(m log(n/m+1)); entropy-potential increases pay for nonoverlapping entries, while an overlap can reduce that potential by only O(log E) per deleted entry. Since each entry is deleted at most once, all melds cost O(E log(E+1)). Destructive trees retain at most E entry nodes, giving linear space.
claims.witness: Invariant: D_C has exactly one representative edge for each box occurring among edges whose targets lie in C; its collisions are precisely the currently enabled congruence implications.
claims.search_method: Proved soundness, terminal stability, event accounting, and the balanced-tree entropy bound independently. The exact checker exhaustively compared the event-driven algorithm with a separate repeated fixed point on 328210 graphs.

claims.claim: Both outcomes have certificates of size O(W+E) verifiable deterministically in O(W+E+B) time.
claims.evidence: For a negative certificate, equality of supplied class numbers defines an equivalence P. Grouping edges by (X,P(t)) and requiring a unique P(o) per group is exactly stability. Since θ is the least stable equivalence, separation under P implies separation under θ; θ itself proves completeness. For a positive certificate, successful folds can be ordered sequentially and there are at most W−1 of them. Representing each successful union by two earlier component roots, two original same-box edges, and an earlier node containing both targets yields a binary merge forest. Induction proves every node's leaves θ-equivalent. A verifier checks the forest structure, edge references, chronology, and four subtree-containment predicates; DFS intervals make containment constant-time. Conversely, any successful folding run produces this forest. Radix grouping for the negative case and one forest traversal for the positive case take O(W+E+B) time and linear space.
claims.witness: Negative instances use P=θ. Positive instances use the chronological forest of successful unions, with the final root containing the start and an accepting wire.
claims.search_method: Proved both soundness and completeness directions and implemented generation plus syntactic verification of merge forests and stable partitions for every one of the 328210 exhaustively enumerated small graphs.

claims.claim: The target O(W+E+B) bound holds for graded dual graphs: graphs admitting an integer rank ρ with ρ(o)=ρ(t)+1 for every edge (o,X,t).
claims.evidence: Induction on closure derivations shows equivalent wires always have equal rank. Consequently, all merges at rank r depend only on already-final equivalence classes at rank r−1. Grouping rank-r edges by (X,class(t)) and taking connected components of the resulting stars therefore gives exactly the final rank-r classes; a later rank cannot create another merge at rank r. Timestamp arrays indexed by boxes and target-class identifiers implement all groups sparsely, touching each edge and wire O(1) times after O(B+W) initialization. Rank existence is checked by propagating the ±1 edge constraints in each weak component. If consistent, componentwise normalization yields a range at most the component size minus one, permitting linear rank buckets. Thus recognition, closure, and the exit query all take O(W+E+B) time and space.
claims.witness: The constructive witness is the increasing-rank component algorithm together with the invariant that rank-r classes are final immediately after processing rank r.
claims.search_method: Proved the rank induction and constraint-propagation argument, exhaustively compared layered closure with unrestricted fixed-point closure on 8721 graded four-wire graphs, and exhaustively checked rank recognition on all 512 three-wire one-box graphs.

claims.claim: Repeated global fixed-point rescanning can require Θ(W) changing rounds even with one box and E=Θ(W).
claims.evidence: In the stated family, round 1 merges only a0 with b0. Inductively, after round k exactly the pairs aj,bj for j<k have merged, so round k+1 enables ak,bk and no higher pair. No cross-level merge is possible because z and distinct levels never acquire equivalent targets. Hence there are n+1 changing rounds for W=2n+3 and E=2n+2. Every changing round reduces the number of classes, giving the matching O(W) upper bound. Assigning a fresh pin to every edge realizes the graph as a well-formed one-box dual maze. A descending level order also forces the same behavior for an in-place scan that does not revisit earlier edges within a pass.
claims.witness: For n=4, use z,a0,b0,…,a4,b4 and edges a0→X z, b0→X z, and ak→X a(k−1), bk→X b(k−1) for 1≤k≤4. This has W=11, E=10, and five changing rounds.
claims.search_method: Proved the round invariant for arbitrary n and ran an exact synchronous-round simulator for all n from 0 through 32, checking the round count and every final equivalence pair.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for an unrestricted O(W+E+B)-time decision algorithm. The draft explicitly does not claim this: its unrestricted deterministic algorithm retains a logarithmic factor, while its linear algorithm applies only to graded dual graphs. Linear certificates do not themselves construct certificates in linear time, and the slow-round example only rules out a particular rescanning strategy. The five verified results are nevertheless material progress toward the target, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate. The draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL and its final writeup state precisely this boundary, making claimed_resolution ACCURATE.
